result:
Your brief has no numbered requirements and no routing header, so I'm treating it and the three research files as background. Every outcome below is a candidate drawn from them, and you confirm which ones stand. I can't write stages until you rank the outcomes, so this message asks for that ranking.

## Candidate outcomes (unranked)

All candidates come from `ces-revisions-prompt.md` unless marked otherwise. Each gets a short tag (Data, Seasonal, and so on) to match the tracks further down. "Revision steps" means the brief's four steps: first→second print, second→third print, third print→benchmark, and post-benchmark/wedge-back.

| # | Outcome | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|
| O1 (Data) | A real-time panel of national CES total nonfarm, SA and NSA. It has first, second and third prints plus preliminary and final benchmarks, so revisions at each step can be read off by month. | Data volume is small: about 1,050 months × a few vintages each. The real cost is assembly before ALFRED's coverage starts. ALFRED's earliest PAYEMS vintage and its vintage count are unknown to me; the probe below answers that. |
| O2 (Data) | The same panel at NAICS supersector detail, SA and NSA. | Unknown. Supersector vintages may need to be pulled from archived Employment Situation releases by hand. Only doing it will tell. |
| O3 (Data) | A descriptive history of revision magnitude at each step over time (dispersion and tails by era, 2003 and 2020–22 marked). | Cheap once O1 exists: minutes of compute. |
| O4 (Seasonal) | A split of SA revisions into an NSA-sample part and a seasonal-factor part, at each of the first two steps. | Needs O1's NSA and SA vintages together. Fit cost is unknown until it runs. |
| O5 (Collection) | An estimate of how collection days (reference week → release) and closing rates move the scale of one-month revisions. | The collection-days covariate is computable from release calendars. Closing-rate history must be gathered from BLS publications; its span is unknown. |
| O6 (Capacity) | Hand-built annual covariates: real BLS appropriations, CR/sequestration/shutdown indicators, FTE, and CES sample size. | Your time. About 40 fiscal years per series from budget justifications and OPM sources. Hours per series are unknown until the first one is built. |
| O7 (Capacity) | Estimates of what those slow covariates do to revision scale, with a plain statement of what ~40 years cannot identify. | Depends on O6 and a fitted scale model. Fit time is unknown until it runs. |
| O8 (State-space) | News-vs-noise shares at each revision step, from a latent true-employment model, with the benchmark as an irregular higher-precision observation and wedge-back. | The NUTS fit cost with the state marginalized is unknown until it runs. |
| O9 (State-space) | Sector-level differences in those effects, partially pooled across supersectors. | Scales with O2 times the O8 fit. Unknown until it runs. |

Qualities to place when the roadmap is written: manifests, traceability, full validation suites, scheduling.

## Proposed tracks

- **A — Vintage data and revision history** (O1, O2, O3): known progression. Its panel is the input every other track reads.
- **B — Seasonal vs sample decomposition** (O4): research. I split it from C–E because its answer stands without any driver estimate.
- **C — Collection interval and revision scale** (O5): research. This is the within-year variation. Its answer stands without the slow covariates.
- **D — Institutional capacity and revision scale** (O6, O7): research. Its covariates are slow-moving and collinear, and its identification story is different from C's, so it shouldn't hold C hostage.
- **E — Multi-vintage news/noise model** (O8, O9): research. This is the brief's full design. B–D's answers don't wait on it, and it can absorb them later.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14 with uv (`.python-version`, `uv.lock`).
- Toolchain from the brief: NumPyro, Dynamax, Blackjax if needed, ArviZ, Polars. Please confirm this is binding.
- The estimand is the scale of revisions, in thousands of jobs, at national CES level.

**Proposed roadmap name:** `ces-revisions`, written to `specs/ces-revisions-roadmap.md`. No file by that name exists.

**Optional probe:** I could fetch ALFRED's vintage list for PAYEMS to firm up O1's cost. It needs your FRED API key, so I'd run it only on your yes.

## One request

Please do three things in one reply:
- Rank the outcomes within each track, and rank the tracks among themselves.
- Confirm or change the tracks and their kinds, including whether B–E should really be separate.
- Confirm the name `ces-revisions` and say whether you want the probe.
